long_biography.plain_text:
Victor Lo helped shape Hong Kong’s M+ museum as chairman of the advisory group that developed its concept. The group visited institutions including the Centre Pompidou, Tate Modern and MoMA, but wanted a broader combination of art, design and moving images. Its proposal treated visual culture across different media as the museum’s organising principle.

His own collecting concentrated on modern Chinese ink painting. He established the M K Lau Collection, named after his late wife, and took his son Alan to exhibitions and auctions. Works from the family collection were displayed in the main dining hall of Duddell’s, the Hong Kong restaurant Alan co-founded.
